slice.intended_test: Test whether a currently Chat-readable GitHub-native provider-controlled event or immutable-object surface can independently retain proof that a newer single-ref transaction existed before a force-capable coherent rewind, without branch/rules administration, organization audit-log authority, manual attestation, hosted compute/storage, external service execution, finite monthly/trial/paid quota, or incremental cost.
observations: GitHub's public REST events documentation exposes repository events and states the endpoint is not built for real-time use; latency can range from about 30 seconds to 6 hours.

GitHub's public event-type documentation defines PushEvent payload fields including push_id, ref, head and before, which is structurally capable of describing that a specific push moved a ref from one SHA to another.

The current connected GitHub generic fetch action rejected a repository-events REST URL as an invalid/unsupported endpoint, so this invocation did not verify a live connector-callable repository-event stream.
A direct generic-web open of the API URL was also unavailable in this run; only the public documentation surface was readable.

No provider durability or indefinite-retention guarantee for repository events was established by the allowed probe. Therefore an event feed cannot yet serve as the required independently retained monotonic witness.

Webhook push payloads also carry before/after SHA information, but a webhook receiver and its durable storage would introduce an external execution/storage authority and is outside the zero-dependency acceptance path.

Immutable Git commit/tree/blob identity alone remains insufficient as a monotonic witness unless there is an independently retained, queryable record that a particular newer transaction existed; this probe established no such provider-retained guarantee.
slice.source_scope: Public GitHub documentation plus current connector/web callability failures only; no O, downstream, other-worker state, other-role receipts, protected/admin settings, live protocol branch mutation, or hosted execution was consumed.

candidate_comparison.repository_events_push_event: Promising provider-generated before/head/push_id structure, but current connector callability was not verified and durable retention/monotonic visibility was not established; fail closed.
candidate_comparison.webhook_push_delivery: Carries before/after but requires external receiver/storage or app-side delivery handling; rejected for the zero-external-execution/storage path.
candidate_comparison.git_immutable_objects_only: Objects are content-addressed, but no independent monotonic existence witness was established after coherent force rewind; insufficient alone.

frontier: Preserve r273 single-ref immutable transaction-record plus force=false ref-update design as the current Chat-callable baseline.
Repository PushEvent has useful before/head/push_id structure, but this run did not establish current connector callability or durable monotonic retention.
Webhook delivery is structurally useful but violates the zero-external-execution/storage path unless a provider-retained query surface can be used directly by Chat.
The decisive unresolved child remains an independently retained monotonic witness for force-capable coherent rewind.
